result.topic_en: The page gives a Lagrange-interpolation-type formula for a polynomial ξ such that ξ·X' − 1 is divisible by X, then an expansion of the function F(x) = ∫(e^x−1)/x dx about a point a, with numerical coefficient tables for a = 1 and a = i and values of F at several real and imaginary points.
result.transcription:
Es sei $X = (x-\alpha)(x-\beta)(x-\gamma)(x-\delta)\ldots\ldots$
und man verlangt eine ganze rationale Function $\xi$, von $x$, eine
Ordnung niedriger als $X$, so dass $\xi\frac{\partial X}{dx} - 1$ durch $X$ theilbar sey.
Man hat wenn man $\frac{\partial X}{\partial x} = X'$ setzt
$\xi = \frac{X}{x-\alpha}\cdot\mathrm{Valor}\ \frac{1}{X'X'}$ pro $x=\alpha$
$+\frac{X}{x-\beta}\cdot\mathrm{Valor}\ \frac{1}{X'X'}$ pro $x=\beta$
$+\frac{X}{x-\gamma}\cdot\mathrm{Valor}\ \frac{1}{X'X'}$ pro $x=\gamma$
$+\frac{X}{x-\delta}\cdot\mathrm{Valor}\ \frac{1}{X'X'}$ pro $x=\delta$
$+$ &c.
Man bemerke, dass der Werth von $X'$ für $x=\alpha$, gleich ist
dem Werthe von $\frac{X}{x-\alpha}$ für $x=\alpha$, oder auch
$= (\alpha-\beta)(\alpha-\gamma)(\alpha-\delta)\ldots\ldots$

Wenn man die Function $\int\frac{e^x-1}{x}\partial x$ durch $\mathfrak{F}x$ bezeichnet, so ist
$\mathfrak{F}x = \mathfrak{F}(x-a) + \log\frac{x-a}{x} + e^{x-a}\left(\frac{A}{x}+\frac{B}{xx}+\frac{C}{x^3}+\frac{D}{x^4}+\&c.\right)$
wo
$A = e^a - 1 = a + \frac{1}{2}aa + \frac{1}{6}a^3 + \frac{1}{24}a^4 + etc.$
$B = A - a = \frac{1}{2}aa + \frac{1}{6}a^3 + \frac{1}{24}a^4 + etc.$
$C = 2B - aa = \frac{1}{3}a^3 + \frac{1}{12}a^4 + etc$
$D = 3C - a^3 = \frac{1}{4}a^4 + etc.$

methods.what: Construction of a polynomial ξ of lower degree than X with ξX' ≡ 1 mod X, via a Lagrange-interpolation-type sum over the roots
Value of the derivative X' at a simple root α equals the product of differences to the other roots
Shift/expansion formula for the integral F(x) = ∫(e^x−1)/x dx in terms of F(x−a), a log term and a series in 1/x
Recursive definition of the coefficients A, B, C, D and their power series in a
Numerical tables of the coefficients for a = 1 and a = i
Numerical values of F at real and imaginary arguments
